data_facts_with_vis_data.paragraph: Even with exercise, sedentary behavior can increase risk of heart failure by up to 60%, according to study

facts.fact_content: Sedentary behavior can increase risk of heart failure by up to 60%.

data_facts_with_vis_data.paragraph: Investigators at Mass General Brigham found sedentary behavior was associated with higher risks of all four types of heart disease, with a marked 40-60 percent greater risk of heart failure and cardiovascular death when sedentary behavior exceeded 10.6 hours a day. (Sedentary behavior is defined as waking activity with low energy expenditure while sitting, reclining, or lying down and does not include hours spent sleeping at night.)

facts.fact_content: 40-60 percent greater risk of heart failure and cardiovascular death when sedentary behavior exceeded 10.6 hours a day.
